description:
Job Title: Head of Channel Sales & Alliances

Location: United States, Remote

This is a fully remote opportunity and can be worked from any location in the United States.

ABOUT THE COMPANY:

Revenue is complex, and clarity is rare. Our mission at Salesloft is to transform revenue complexity into clear, decisive action for every team driving growth.

We’re building the industry’s first Predictive Revenue System, where humans and AI work together to make confident decisions based on real signals. Thousands of customers run on our platforms every day, which gives us Revenue Context: a view into what happens in a deal, when, and with what outcome.

Our vision is a future where revenue growth is predictable and the teams driving it are unstoppable. If you want to help build it, alongside people who Move as One and let Evidence over Ego guide the work, we’d love to meet you.

THE OPPORTUNITYOwn the partner channel that sources a meaningful share of Salesloft’s new closed-won revenue.

As our Head of Channel Sales & Alliances, you'll build and run a quota-carrying Channel Sales & Alliances organization focused on four motions: private equity partnerships, cloud marketplace and strategic platform alliances, ISV and MCP partnerships, and VAR, BPO, and services partnerships. The primary measure is closed-won revenue sourced through partners, supported by partner-influenced revenue and the retention and expansion of partner-sourced customers. Relationships, programs, and pipelines are critical in producing signed deals. You will be the executive face of Salesloft to our most strategic partners and the owner of the plan, the team, and the results.

On a day-to-day basis, you will:

Private Equity Partnerships

  • Build relationships with private equity firms and their operating partners to position Salesloft as the revenue platform for their portfolio companies.
  • Structure portfolio-wide agreements and programs that turn a firm-level relationship into sourced, closed-won deals across multiple portfolio companies.
  • Work with Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success to run portfolio-specific plays, from the initial introduction through close.

Cloud Marketplace and Strategic Platform Alliances

  • Own Salesloft's go-to-market with AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud, including marketplace listings, private offers, and co-sell programs that let customers buy against their existing cloud commitments.
  • Build strategic alliances with the CRM and productivity platforms our customers run on, such as Salesforce, Microsoft, and HubSpot, including their app and agent marketplaces.
  • Turn platform relationships into sourced and co-sold pipeline by aligning with these partners' field sellers, not only their partner teams.

ISV and MCP Partnerships

  • Identify, recruit, and sign independent software vendors and AI platforms that integrate with, embed, or distribute Salesloft, including through MCP (Model Context Protocol) integrations and agent ecosystems.
  • Define co-sell and co-marketing motions with ISV partners so that integrations produce sourced pipeline and closed-won revenue, not only technical listings.
  • Work with Product and Engineering to shape the partner integration roadmap and make sure partners can build, launch, and sell with confidence.
  • Design partner economics for AI and agent partners, including revenue share on usage- and consumption-based pricing alongside seat-based models.

VAR, BPO, and Services Partnerships

  • Recruit and onboard value-added resellers and business process outsourcing providers that resell, bundle, or deliver Salesloft as part of their sales services.
  • Recruit systems integrators and RevOps consultancies that influence enterprise buying decisions and deliver implementations, and build a services partner motion that speeds time to value and improves retention.
  • Negotiate reseller and partner agreements, pricing, margin structures, and business terms that support profitable, repeatable revenue.
  • Equip partner sellers with value-selling playbooks, competitive positioning, and qualification criteria so deals are sourced and closed consistently.

HOW YOU’LL WORK HERE

  • Move as One: You’ll partner with Sales, Marketing, Product, Customer Success, Legal, and RevOps on joint plays and partner attribution, and share credit for partner-sourced wins.
  • Evidence over Ego: You’ll plan, forecast, and report on partner-sourced and partner-influenced revenue using real signals, and say so when the data changes your mind.
  • Lead from the Front: You’ll be the executive face of Salesloft to strategic partners and set the quotas, coverage models, and standards your team is held to.
  • Make Your Mark: You’ll shape how Salesloft shows up in private equity, cloud marketplaces, ISV and MCP ecosystems, and services channels, not just run the playbook.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FORYou’re a senior partner and alliances leader who has sourced and closed partner-driven revenue in B2B SaaS and led teams to quota. You build the relationships and programs that turn into signed deals, and you are credible with C-level partners and technical teams alike. If you want to learn more, do more, and become more, this is your next move.

YOU’LL BRING

  • 12+ years of experience in partner sales, channel sales, alliances, or business development in B2B SaaS, with senior leadership experience managing teams
  • A track record of sourcing and closing partner-driven revenue and meeting or exceeding quota, with results you can describe in terms of closed-won revenue
  • Experience building or working with private equity relationships, ISV or technology integration partnerships, cloud marketplace and co-sell programs with AWS, Microsoft, or Google Cloud, or VAR, BPO, and services channel programs. Experience in more than one of these is strongly preferred
  • Experience building a partner program from the ground up, or rebuilding one after a merger or acquisition
  • An established network of private equity operating partners and portfolio company leaders
  • Familiarity with AI, API, and MCP-based integration ecosystems, and the ability to talk credibly with technical partners about how Salesloft fits
  • Proven ability to negotiate complex partner, reseller, and revenue-sharing agreements
  • Ability to coach and lead a team, including setting quotas and holding people accountable to them
  • Strong sales acumen and fluency with CRM and partner tools such as Salesforce, partner relationship management platforms, and account-mapping tools, including building partner attribution models. SaaS experience is required
  • Executive presence, including comfort presenting at conferences, events, and webinars and influencing C-suite stakeholders
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, and the ability to lead cross-functional initiatives across Product, Marketing, and Revenue teams

THE TEAMYou’ll lead the Channel Sales & Alliances team of partner sales and alliance professionals and work closely with Sales, Marketing, Product, Customer Success, Legal, and RevOps. It’s a place to grow as the executive owner of a channel plan, a team, and the results.

BENEFITS:

title: Compliance Officer (Remote/Virtual, IN, US)
description:
The Opportunity

Purdue Global is seeking an accomplished, forward-thinking Compliance Officer to provide leadership for the university’s compliance, ethics, and enterprise risk management programs.

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer and maintaining a collaborative relationship with the Chief Counsel, the Compliance Officer will serve as a strategic advisor to the CEO and university leadership. This individual will establish, guide, and maintain a comprehensive compliance, ethics, and risk mitigation program that supports Purdue Global’s mission while aligning with the Purdue system’s enterprise-wide compliance framework.

The Compliance Officer will provide leadership across a complex regulatory landscape that includes federal and state higher education requirements, accreditation, educational technology governance, data privacy, accessibility, multi-state employment compliance, and enterprise risk management. The successful candidate will bring sound judgment, executive presence, and the ability to translate evolving regulatory requirements into practical institutional strategies.

Key Responsibilities

Regulatory and Statutory Compliance

  • Direct and oversee compliance strategies related to federal and state higher education regulations.
  • Provide institutional leadership regarding Title IV financial aid regulations, Title IX, the Violence Against Women Act, FERPA, and consumer protection disclosure requirements.
  • Oversee compliance with State Authorization Reciprocity Agreements and other multi-state authorization requirements affecting online education.
  • Monitor federal and state legislative and regulatory developments and lead proactive institutional responses.
  • Coordinate compliance activities involving the U.S. Department of Education, Office for Civil Rights, Indiana Commission for Higher Education, state workforce agencies, and other regulatory bodies.

Enterprise Risk Management and Policy Leadership

  • Design, implement, and lead the university’s enterprise risk management practices in alignment with Purdue system frameworks.
  • Identify and assess operational, cybersecurity, financial, academic, regulatory, and reputational risks.
  • Collaborate with Purdue system Risk Management and Internal Audit teams.
  • Develop compliance dashboards, risk registers, and key risk indicators that support timely decision-making and proactive mitigation.
  • Connect risk indicators with Purdue Global quality assurance measures and strategic academic and operational initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

Emerging Technology and Digital Learning Governance

  • Participate in enterprise processes that establish and maintain compliance frameworks for artificial intelligence and machine learning in academic and administrative operations.
  • Provide leadership regarding artificial intelligence ethics, educational technology governance, and responsible institutional use.
  • Champion digital accessibility requirements, including the Americans with Disabilities Act, Sections 504 and 508, and Web Content Accessibility Guidelines.
  • Monitor student and employee data privacy requirements under FERPA, state privacy laws, and applicable international frameworks such as the General Data Protection Regulation.
  • Partner with the Chief Information Officer and other leaders to address risks associated with remote proctoring, biometric and related data, cloud-hosted instructional tools, and emerging technologies.

Accreditation

  • Partner with the Chief Academic Officer, academic deans, and accreditation liaisons to support continued compliance with institutional and programmatic accreditation requirements.
  • Support compliance with Higher Learning Commission expectations and specialized accrediting bodies.
  • Ensure adherence to federal distance education requirements, including Regular and Substantive Interaction standards.

Audits, Investigations, and Employment Compliance

  • Direct institutional preparation and response for federal compliance audits, annual Single Audits, state agency reviews, and independent evaluations.
  • Oversee responses to reports received through the university’s anonymous whistleblower hotline.
  • Direct objective, timely, and legally sound reviews of reported noncompliance.
  • Collaborate with Human Resources on multi-state employment compliance for a distributed workforce, including requirements under the Fair Labor Standards Act, Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs, and Americans with Disabilities Act.

Executive Advising and Leadership

  • Serve as a trusted compliance and risk advisor to the CEO and university leadership.
  • Prepare and present executive summaries, compliance dashboards, quarterly risk registers, and recommendations to the CEO, university board, and Core Leadership Team.
  • Lead and develop a multidisciplinary team of compliance directors and specialists.
  • Navigate sensitive academic and administrative matters with discretion, diplomacy, and sound judgment.

Required Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in higher education administration, public policy, business administration, or a closely related field.
  • Ten years of progressively responsible leadership experience in compliance, regulatory affairs, legal services, or risk management.
  • At least five years of senior-level leadership experience within a higher education environment.
  • Significant experience interpreting and applying U.S. Department of Education regulations, including Title IV, FERPA, and Title IX.
  • Experience with multi-state authorization requirements affecting online or distance education.
  • Demonstrated experience leading multidisciplinary teams and managing long-term operational and strategic initiatives.
  • Experience designing or coordinating enterprise risk management frameworks in collaboration with internal audit, legal, risk management, or related university functions.
  • Strong executive communication, negotiation, mediation, and advisory skills.
  • Ability to manage confidential matters and navigate complex academic and administrative decision-making processes.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Juris Doctor degree.
  • Advanced knowledge of accreditation, online education, and distance learning regulatory requirements.
  • Experience with educational technology governance, artificial intelligence and machine learning compliance, data privacy, and digital accessibility standards.
  • Experience developing executive-level risk registers, compliance dashboards, and key risk indicators.

What you'll do at Jamf:

The Senior Sales Compensation Analyst drives the day-to-day sales compensation operations for Jamf's global sales organization and serves as the technical and modeling lead for the team. This role supports monthly commission controls, commission platform administration and commission plan modeling. The Senior Sales Compensation Analyst works closely with Finance, Sales Leadership, Sales Operations, Legal, and HR to design plans that motivate our sales teams, keep incentive cost predictable.

What you can expect to do in this role:

  • Own the monthly commission close and annual plan calendar, setting priorities across controls, CaptivateIQ updates, and model deadlines.

  • Resolve commission inquiries and disputes, report monthly inquiry metrics to improve plans, communications, and training.
  • Support the sales compensation exception (SSE) review process and ticket resolution, including windfall and off-cycle compensation cases. Prepare formal compensation treatment memos for leadership.
  • Build and maintain reporting and forecasting tools and serve as the primary sales compensation data partner to Revenue Operations, including Domo dashboards, source data validation, and the plan rule documentation.
  • Build and maintain multi-scenario Excel models that evaluate plan structures (quota credit, accelerators, quota amplifiers, gates, and caps) against incentive cost, rep earnings, attainment distribution, and quota-to-OTE ratios.
  • Support the annual sales compensation plan proposal but validating assumptions against prior-year actuals, tying model outputs to leadership materials, and contributing recommendations to Finance and Sales leadership.
  • Serve as a mentor and help train junior analysts on CaptivateIQ, plan modeling, and audit procedures. Support the Senior Manager in onboarding new team members.
  • Develop field-facing communications, including plan documents, FAQs, talk tracks, and office hours materials, that explain plan mechanics and changes to sales leaders and reps, and present complex analysis to executives.
  • Identify and implement process improvements that increase accuracy, automate repeatable work, and strengthen controls over compensation operations, including SOX-relevant processes.

What we are looking for:

  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in Total Rewards, sales compensation, or incentive compensation, including direct experience with commission plan modeling (Required)
  • Working knowledge of SQL for extracting and validating commission data and experience with Python or openpyxl for file processing or validation (Required).
  • Understanding of financial controls and audit requirements, including SOX and familiarity with commission accounting under ASC 340-40. (Required)
  • Sound judgement and discretion with confidential compensation matters. (Required)
  • Demonstrated analytical skills and attention to detail across multiple files and presentations before sign-off. (Required)
  • Advanced, hands-on proficiency with CaptivateIQ or a comparable incentive compensation platform, including configuring incentive plans, building calculation logic, managing data loads, and troubleshooting calculation results. (Preferred)
  • Excel modeling skills, including multi-scenario models with built-in validation checks, checks and testing for unintended outcomes such as windfalls or plan gaming. (Preferred)
  • Working knowledge of sales compensation plan design, including quota setting, accelerators, decelerators, caps, gates, multipliers, SPIFs, and kickers along with sales alignment and territory planning. (Preferred)
  • Working knowledge of the Salesforce and Workday data structures used in sales compensation, such as opportunities, bookings, quotas, territories, and organizational hierarchies. (Preferred)

EDUCATION AND CERTIFICATIONS

  • 4 Year / Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or other business-related field (Required)
  • A combination of relevant experience and education may be considered

SECURITY AND PRIVACY REQUIREMENTS

title: New Business Manager
description:
Our company

Surfer is an AI Visibility Platform that helps marketing teams become the definitive answer wherever their buyers search — across Google and AI search. The platform combines data, research-backed optimization, and a user-friendly workflow to grow brand visibility through content where buying decisions start to form.

Surfer is used by content marketers, SEO specialists, agencies, and in-house marketing teams around the world to track, plan, write, and optimize content that gets ranked and cited by both search engines and LLMs.

Surfer is part of Positive Group - a fast-growing tech group specializing in B2B SaaS products that help marketing teams grow smarter. The group brings together several brands around a common ambition: to become the European benchmark in MarTech. With around 400 employees based in France, Germany, Italy, and Poland, Positive supports customers in 80+ countries.

We’re a remote-first company, but if you ever crave some in-person energy, we’ve got a cozy office in Wrocław , Poland where the magic happens (and coffee never runs out ☕).


About the role

We're looking for someone who's worked at a marketing/SEO agency or a martech company and knows what it takes to close - someone who picks up the phone without thinking twice, and who hasn't been trained out of that instinct by years of "process."

On a day-to-day basis, you'll own the new-business side end-to-end: prospecting and building your own pipeline, working the leads that come your way, qualifying them, running discovery and demos, negotiating, and closing. You'll work closely with the Customer Success team, and get support from Marketing and RevOps. This role rewards initiative - the more you build and close, the more it shows, both in your results and in what you earn.

You will be responsible for:

  • Work both sides of the pipeline: reaching out to existing leads in our CRM (conference, meetup, webinar, and community signals plus records of past interest) while building a new pipeline from scratch through your own outbound prospecting.

  • Prospect actively: research target accounts, identify decision-makers, and open conversations with agencies and in-house teams that haven’t reached out to us yet.

  • Run multi-channel outreach on these leads across email, LinkedIn, and phone.

  • Build and continuously refine ICP-aligned contact lists covering both marketing/SEO agencies and in-house SEO/marketing teams at companies.

  • Qualify leads and run discovery calls, demos, and negotiations, owning the deal through to signed contract and payment.

Requirements:

  • Minimum 4 years of B2B sales experience as an SDR/BDR/AE at a marketing/SEO agency, a martech company (e.g. SEO, content, analytics, or marketing automation software), or at a company selling into agencies.

  • Proven track record of closing deals end-to-end, including negotiation and contracting.

  • Familiarity with the SEO/content marketing space (content briefs, topical authority, SERPs).

  • No hesitation picking up the phone the moment a lead is worth chasing.

  • Motivated by closing deals, not just running a process. You know the satisfaction of seeing a deal through from first call to signed contract - and you want more of that.

  • Outreach experience across email, LinkedIn, and phone.

  • Familiarity with CRM and sales/outbound tools.

  • Strong written and verbal English (C1 or above).

  • Nice to have: experience selling a SaaS product (not a service); ABM (account-based marketing/sales) experience.

What we offer:

We build the team around experts and stay out of their way. That starts with the basics:

Compensation: $36,000–45,500/year base (excl. VAT, where applicable), plus a bonus system.

Contract: We work exclusively on B2B (contractor) agreements. This means you’ll need your own registered business (e.g. sole proprietorship / self-employed status in your country) and will invoice us monthly.

We take care of the things that matter outside the work itself - your health, your rest, the setup that lets you work well, and the chance to sharpen your craft. Everything else follows from how we operate: trust over control, outcomes over hours.

Location and Remote Work:

We’re a remote-first company, but if you ever crave some in-person energy, we’ve got a cozy office in Wrocław, Poland.

title: Quality Assurance Rater - Spanish speakers in Spain
description:
Join our elite team of Senior Raters as a critical contributor to high-quality validation data that directly influences product development and quality assurance for leading search engines and AI technologies.

This flexible, remote opportunity allows you to apply your analytical and research skills to evaluate search results and AI-generated content while contributing to the development of high-quality AI systems.

 

A Day in the Life of a Quality Assurance Rater

In this role, you'll conduct analytical assessments of search results and AI responses, providing ratings and feedback that help improve AI model performance and search quality.

Your work will maintain high quality standards and deliver the accuracy our clients depend on.

You'll evaluate a variety of rating tasks, analyze content with attention to detail, conduct research to support rating decisions, and identify guideline gaps or task inconsistencies.

You'll also participate in training and calibration sessions while contributing feedback to improve rating processes and guidelines.

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Evaluate search results and AI-generated content for quality, relevance, accuracy, and usefulness.
  • Conduct online research to verify information and support rating decisions.
  • Apply rating guidelines consistently while maintaining quality standards.
  • Document edge cases, guideline gaps, and task-related issues.
  • Provide clear written feedback and rationale for ratings when required.
  • Participate in training, calibration sessions, and ongoing quality reviews.
  • Meet productivity expectations while maintaining high-quality work.

 

TELUS Digital AI Community

Our global AI Community is a vibrant network of 1 million+ contributors from diverse backgrounds who help our customers collect, enhance, train, translate, and localize content to build better AI models. Become part of our growing community and make an impact supporting the machine learning models of some of the world’s largest brands. 

Qualification path

 

Candidates will complete project-specific training and qualification assessments before joining the program. Ongoing work will be subject to regular quality assurance reviews and performance monitoring.

 

Basic Requirements

  • Working as a freelancer with excellent communication skills in Spanish & English.
  • Resident in Spain for the last 5 consecutive years.
  • Familiarity with current and historical business, media, sports, news, social media, and cultural affairs.
  • Strong analytical thinking, attention to detail, and research skills.
  • Experience using web browsers, search engines, and online research tools.
  • Daily access to a reliable broadband internet connection, smartphone, and personal computer.
  • Demonstrated research capability through professional background OR strong track record of self-directed research and information verification
  • Ability to work independently and follow detailed guidelines consistently.
  • High level of creativity and logical skills with the ability to achieve consistent targets

 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in quality assurance, content moderation, data annotation, research, journalism, editing, or information verification.
  • Familiarity with AI technologies, search engines, and digital content ecosystems.
  • Subject matter expertise in areas such as Popular Culture, Social Sciences, STEM, Medicine, Law, Finance, or Engineering.
  • Additional language skills may be beneficial depending on project requirements.

 

Equal Opportunity

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for a contractual relationship without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status. At TELUS Digital AI, we are proud to offer equal opportunities and are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive community. All aspects of selection are based on applicants’ qualifications, merits, competence, and performance without regard to any characteristic related to diversity.
